parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Given that 75% of the candidates passed the examination, state the lowest mark for the award of a pass.
(1)

(a) [pass for] 30 (labelled or 1st answer) B1

parts.label: b

(c) Find the value of $c$ and the value of $d$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:

1st B1 for $c=70$; 2nd B1 for $d=6$ (Allow B1B1 for unlabelled 70 followed by 6)
SC Award B1B0 for $c=6$ and $d=70$ or $6$ and $70$ in the wrong order

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Write down the 3 highest marks scored in the examination.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) 68, 72, 79 B2/1/0
B2 for all 3 correct values (and no extra value) (B1 for two correct)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- In (a), (b), (c) and (d) condone correct numbers with % e.g. 30% for (a)

parts.label: e
parts.text:

(e) On the diagram on page 7, complete the box and whisker plot.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) 5 < d therefore 5 is an outlier M1
[Fully correct box plot drawn with outlier at 5 marked and single lower whisker stopping at 10] A1, A1
M1 for identifying or stating (e.g. on the grid) that 5 is the only outlier or lower whisker ending at 6 or 10 (may be implied by a correct diagram)
1st A1 for only one outlier correctly marked at 5 (whisker(s) must stop above 5)
2nd A1 for a single lower whisker stopping at 10 (2 whiskers is A0 here)

If the outlier is at 5 and lower whisker ends at 6 award M1A1A0
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Fully correct box plot scores M1A1A1

parts.label: f
parts.text:
Three candidates are selected at random from those who took this examination.
(f) Find the probability that all 3 of these candidates passed the examination but only 2 achieved a merit grade.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(f) $\frac{1}{2}\times\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^2\times 3 = \frac{3}{32}$ M1M1, A1
1st M1 for $\frac{1}{2}\times\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^2$
2nd M1 for an expression of the form $pq^2\times 3$ where $p$ and $q$ are probabilities ($p\neq q$)
NB $\frac{3}{4}\times\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^2\times 3 = \frac{9}{64} = 0.140625$ is a common incorrect answer and scores M0M1A0

questions.stem:
A training agency awards a certificate to each student who passes a test while completing a course.
Students failing the test will attempt the test again up to 3 more times, and, if they pass the test, will be awarded a certificate.
The probability of passing the test at the first attempt is 0.7, but the probability of passing reduces by 0.2 at each attempt.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Complete the tree diagram below to show this information.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) 1st B1 for correctly placing 0.3 and 0.5
2nd B1 for correctly placing 0.7, 0.1 and 0.9

parts.label: b
parts.text:
A student who completed the course is selected at random.
(b) Find the probability that the student was awarded a certificate.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $1-0.3\times 0.5\times 0.7\times 0.9$ or $0.7+(0.3\times 0.5)+(0.3\times 0.5\times 0.3)+(0.3\times 0.5\times 0.7\times 0.1)$ M1
$=0.9055$ A1
Apart from (d), a correct answer with no incorrect working scores full marks.
M1 for a correct expression (ft from their tree diagram)
A1 for 0.9055 or exact equivalent e.g. $\frac{1811}{2000}$. Accept 0.906 only if correct expression seen

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Given that the student was awarded a certificate, find the probability that the student passed on the first or second attempt.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $[\mathrm{P}(P_1\cup P_2|\text{Pass})=]\ \dfrac{0.7+\text{"}0.3\text{"}\times 0.5}{(b)} = \dfrac{0.85}{\text{"}0.9055\text{"}}$ M1, A1ft
$=0.938707...=$ awrt $0.939$ A1
M1 for a correct ratio of probs ft their 0.3 and their answer to (b) [if <1]. Num > Den M0
A1ft for correct numerator and their part (b) on denominator
A1 for awrt 0.939 or accept exact fraction e.g. $\frac{1700}{1811}$

parts.label: d
parts.text:
The training agency decides to alter the test taken by the students while completing the course, but will not allow more than 2 attempts. The agency requires the probability of passing the test at the first attempt to be $p$, and the probability of passing the test at the second attempt to be $(p-0.2)$. The percentage of students who complete the course and are awarded a certificate is to be 95%
(d) Show that $p$ satisfies the equation
$p^2 - 2.2p + 1.15 = 0$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) $p+(1-p)(p-0.2)$ or $1-(1-p)(1.2-p)$ (o.e.) M1
e.g. $p+p-p^2+0.2p-0.2=0.95 \rightarrow p^2-2.2p+1.15=0$ (*) dM1, A1cso
1st M1 for a correct expression for P(pass) in terms of $p$ [condone $p-(p-1)(p-0.2)$ etc]
2nd dM1 dep. on 1st M1 for expanding brackets and forming an equation in $p$. Allow one slip
A1cso correct processing leading to printed answer. No incorrect working seen.

parts.label: e
parts.text:
(e) Hence find the value of $p$, giving your answer to 3 decimal places.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) $p = \dfrac{2.2\pm\sqrt{2.2^2-4\times 1.15}}{2}$ or Complete the square: $(p-1.1)^2-1.1^2+1.15=0$ M1
$=\dfrac{2.2\pm 0.4898...}{2}$ or $\dfrac{2.2\pm\sqrt{0.24}}{2}$ or $1.1\pm\sqrt{0.06}$ or $(1.34...), 0.855...$ A1
$p=0.85505102...$ $p=0.855$ A1
M1 for attempt to solve given equation, correct expression. Condone just $+$ not $\pm$
1st A1 for correct expression and simplified square root or $1.34...$ and $0.855...$
2nd A1 for $p=0.855$ only (penalise any extra value >1). Correct answer only scores 3/3
For $\frac{1}{10}(11-\sqrt{6})$ or $0.855...$ score M1A1A0 (not to 3dp) but for $0.855$ can score M1A1A1

questions.stem: Rosie keeps bees. The amount of honey, in kg, produced by a hive of Rosie's bees in a season, is modelled by a normal distribution with a mean of 22 kg and a standard deviation of 10 kg.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the probability that a hive of Rosie's bees produces less than 18 kg of honey in a season.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $[\mathrm{P}(H<18)=]\ \mathrm{P}\left(Z<\dfrac{18-22}{10}\right)=\mathrm{P}(Z<-0.4)$ M1
$=1-0.6554$ dM1
$=0.3446$ or awrt $0.345$ A1
1st M1 for standardising with 18, 22 and 10. Allow $\pm\dfrac{18-22}{10}$
2nd dM1 dependent on 1st M1 for $1-p$ where $0.6<p<0.7$
A1 for 0.3446 or better or awrt 0.345. NB Calculator gives 0.3445783... Ans only 3/3

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The local bee keepers' club awards a certificate to every hive that produces more than 39 kg of honey in a season, and a medal to every hive that produces more than 50 kg in a season. Given that one of Rosie's bee hives is awarded a certificate
(b) find the probability that this hive is also awarded a medal.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\mathrm{P}(H>50)=\mathrm{P}(Z>2.8)=1-0.9974=0.0026$ M1, A1
$\mathrm{P}(H>39)=\mathrm{P}(Z>1.7)=1-0.9554=0.0446$ M1, A1
$\mathrm{P}(H>50\mid H>39)=\dfrac{\mathrm{P}(H>50)}{\mathrm{P}(H>39)}$ or $\dfrac{\text{"}0.0026\text{"}}{\text{"}0.0446\text{"}}$ M1
$=0.057\sim 0.0585$ A1
1st M1 for correct standardisation and $1-q$ (where $q=0.9...$) for one of these probs
1st A1 for 0.0026 or better (calc 0.0025551...) or $1-0.9974$ (or better)
2nd A1 for 0.0446 or better (calc 0.0445654...) or $1-0.9554$ (or better)
2nd M1 for a correct ratio of probability expressions or values (ft their 0.0026 and 0.0446 but if num.>denom. then M0)
3rd A1 for answer in the range 0.057~0.0585. No fractions but $\frac{13}{223}$ can score M1A1A1M1A0
Ans. only: Can score full marks for either awrt 0.0583 (tables) or awrt 0.0573 (calc) only

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Sam also keeps bees. The amount of honey, in kg, produced by a hive of Sam's bees in a season, is modelled by a normal distribution with mean $\mu$ kg and standard deviation $\sigma$ kg. The probability that a hive of Sam's bees produces less than 28 kg of honey in a season is 0.8413
Only 20% of Sam's bee hives produce less than 18 kg of honey in a season.
(c) Find the value of $\mu$ and the value of $\sigma$. Give your answers to 2 decimal places.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:

$\dfrac{28-\mu}{\sigma}=1$ A1

$\sigma=$ awrt $5.43$ A1
$\mu=$ awrt $22.57$ A1

B1 for using $z=0.8416$ or better (allow $\pm$). Calculator gives 0.8416212...
1st A1 for both equations with $\pm 1$ and $\pm 0.84$ or better
SC for $\dfrac{28-\mu}{\sigma}=\pm 0.8416$ and $\dfrac{18-\mu}{\sigma}=\pm 1$ award M1B1A0 (0.84 instead of 0.8416 loses B1)
2nd M1 for solving their linear equations in $\mu$ & $\sigma$. Reducing to an equation in one variable. Correct processes allow one sign slip

3rd A1 for $\mu=$ awrt 22.57
Calc: No $z=0.8416$ or better seen: can award 6/6 for $\sigma=$ awrt 5.4300 or 5.4301 and $\mu=$ awrt 22.57
No working: For $\sigma=$ awrt 5.43 and $\mu=$ awrt 22.57 award M1B0A1M1A1A1 i.e. 5/6
